findings.name: shadcn/ui + Radix + Tailwind v4

findings.name: zustand + zundo (undo/redo)
findings.what_it_does: zustand 5.0.15: tiny hook-based store with selectors and persist, devtools and immer middleware. zundo 2.3.0 (github.com/charkour/zundo, MIT, under 700 B) adds undo/redo for zustand v5 with partialize, limit and pause/resume.
findings.how_we_use_it: One store for graph, run results, assumption registry and FALSE ASSUMPTION flags. Wrap with zundo; partialize so only nodes, edges and assumptions enter history, not run results. persist saves projects to IndexedDB. Keep module logic outside React.

findings.name: xyflow / React Flow 12 (@xyflow/react) + React Flow UI
findings.what_it_does: Node-based UI library: custom node components, multiple handles with unique ids, minimap, controls. React Flow UI offers shadcn-based copy-paste parts (Base Node, Labeled Handle, Zoom Slider, Node Search) and an AI Workflow Editor template.
findings.how_we_use_it: Each module is a custom node; port types encoded in handle ids and checked with isValidConnection on the ReactFlow component; categories as node colour; run-all or step-in via our own executor (topological sort with dirty-flag cache). Define nodeTypes outside components.
findings.saves: Weeks of canvas, pan/zoom, edge routing and selection work; Grasshopper-like feel from day one.
findings.risks: Keep the attribution badge: maintainers ask for a Pro subscription to remove it (a request; MIT does not require it). UI only: typed-port rules, executor and undo are ours (about 2 person-days). Pro templates are paid. No JavaScript typed-handle example found.

findings.name: NodePen (nodepen/nodes): Grasshopper web client, prior art
findings.what_it_does: MIT open-source node viewer library behind NodePen, a web client for Grasshopper (topics nextjs, rhinocompute). A document is JSON nodes that reference templates by id; the 3D viewer is named Selva. 184 stars, 2 open issues, 2,774 commits.
findings.how_we_use_it: Study, do not depend: borrow the template-plus-document JSON split (our manifest plus graph file) and Grasshopper parameter conventions. Optional half-day spike to see whether its viewer could render our typed-port nodes; otherwise stay on xyflow.
findings.license: MIT (shown on the repo page; licence text not read)
findings.last_activity: main last commit 2026-10-19 (Dependabot merges, commits Atom feed); round 1 noted release 2.0.0 on 2 Oct 2026 (not re-confirmed)
findings.maintainer: NodePen project (README credits contributors and a Glide sponsorship)
findings.saves: Design time on Grasshopper-like node and parameter conventions; a proven JSON template/document schema for graphs.
findings.risks: Offline demo is viewer-only: solving needs Rhino Compute or Grasshopper, not our modules. Typed-port rendering and npm API are undocumented in the README. Next.js app and low stars, though commits are active.

findings.name: Observable Plot
findings.what_it_does: Layered-marks charting library for tabular data with SVG output. Latest release 0.6.17 was published 14 Feb 2025 (npm time); the April 2026 dates are later metadata edits, not a new release. ISC licence.
findings.how_we_use_it: Default chart library for module result cards and the four A2 boards, written as small spec functions returning SVG; wrap in one React component. Colour scales follow a single design-token palette. Spike the board export in week 1 (see Playwright finding).
findings.last_activity: main last commit 2026-09-01; npm 0.6.17 published 2025-02-14 (npm 'modified' 2026-04-06; releases feed entry updated 2026-04-12; no newer version)
findings.saves: About 5-15 lines per chart so Claude writes and edits charts cheaply; vector SVG suits print boards.
findings.risks: 0.x API may change; last release is 20 months old but main is active. No official React bindings; wrapper, SVG export and bundle size need a spike. Less built-in interactivity than ECharts.

findings.name: Vega-Lite (and Vega) for community chart specs
findings.what_it_does: Declarative JSON grammar compiling to Vega. vega-lite 6.5.0 (8 Oct 2026, needs Node 22+), vega 6.4.0, vega-embed 7.3.0 (bundles vega-interpreter). Vega lists 10 security advisories, three rated High since Nov 2025.
findings.how_we_use_it: Accept community charts only as host-defined chart templates plus validated data, never raw specs. If raw specs are ever allowed: schema-validate, block data.url with a custom loader, keep vega-functions 6.1.1 or later (6.2.0 now), render inside the sandbox iframe. Plot stays default.
findings.saves: Spec-as-data is diffable and reviewable on GitHub; Claude writes valid specs reliably, if templates keep the surface small.
findings.risks: CSP-safe vega-interpreter does NOT stop CVE-2025-66648 (setdata XSS, fixed in vega-functions 6.1.1). Bundle size unverified; builds need Node 22+; less ergonomic than Plot for bespoke board graphics.

findings.name: three.js + @react-three/fiber 9 + drei (3D viewport)

findings.how_we_use_it: Viewport for imported and modelled massing, context blocks, solar overlays and board screenshots. Pin R3F 9.x (v10 is alpha) and React ~19.3.1 together and group their Dependabot updates. Load OBJ/glTF with three addons; convert .3dm meshes from the rhino3dm worker; keep geometry as plain data outside React.
findings.popularity: three.js 116.7k stars (14.1M weekly npm); R3F 33.1k; drei about 10.0k
findings.saves: Weeks of viewer, picking, camera and loader work; huge public corpus, so Claude usually writes correct three.js code first time (inference).
findings.risks: R3F 9.8.2 rejects React 19.4 (peer range), so install fails when React moves. R3F v10 alpha is WebGPU-first: stay on 9.x. Large meshes need instancing and BVH. WebGL canvas tests are flaky. No CSG or IFC built in.

findings.name: rhino3dm (rhino3dm.js / Python)
findings.what_it_does: Reads and writes Rhino .3dm files without Rhino via OpenNURBS; JavaScript/WebAssembly package on npm, Python wheels, .NET. Heavy operations delegate to Rhino Compute.
findings.how_we_use_it: Import .3dm massing in a Web Worker, convert to meshes for three.js, read layers as program tags. Cohort tools dtmass and Vista read .3dm in-browser; study that pattern, but copy no code until their licences are granted.
findings.saves: Weeks versus writing a .3dm parser; proven in browser by cohort tools and an IAAC collaborative prototype.
findings.risks: WASM download size; no rendering (needs three.js); Rhino-version file compatibility; advanced geometry operations need Rhino Compute (server). Covers only one of five promised import formats.

findings.name: web-ifc + That Open Components (IFC import)
findings.what_it_does: web-ifc 0.0.78 (21 Sep 2026) reads and writes IFC in WebAssembly, with single- and multi-thread builds. @thatopen/components 3.4.9 (MIT) adds three.js-based BIM tools: dimensions, floorplan navigation, DXF export.
findings.how_we_use_it: v1 IFC import: parse in a worker, convert to meshes, read storeys and spaces as program tags. Revit and SketchUp users export IFC (or OBJ/glTF) following a one-page guide. Use web-ifc alone first; add components only if clipping or measuring is needed.
findings.popularity: web-ifc 1.1k stars (about 151k weekly npm); components 716 stars
findings.last_activity: web-ifc commit 2026-10-19, release 0.78 on 2026-09-21; components 3.4.9 on 2026-10-06
findings.saves: Weeks versus writing an IFC parser; same stack as the viewer; keeps Revit and SketchUp users in the workflow.
findings.risks: MPL-2.0 is file-level copyleft: keep web-ifc unmodified. 0.0.x API may change. Multithread build needs SharedArrayBuffer (COOP and COEP headers; a Workers host or coi-serviceworker). IFC quality varies by exporter; 70 open issues.

findings.name: manifold-3d (mesh booleans for massing edits)
findings.what_it_does: manifold-3d 3.5.4 (25 Sep 2026): WebAssembly build of a geometry library with guaranteed-manifold mesh booleans; also volume and surface-area queries. Commits to 20 Oct 2026.
findings.how_we_use_it: v1 massing edits: union, subtract and setback booleans for podium and tower stacks, plus volume and area for FAR and GFA checks. For 13 Nov use simple extruded footprints without booleans.
findings.saves: Robust booleans (the hardest part of in-browser modelling) instead of a hand-written CSG kernel; weeks of edge-case debugging avoided.
findings.risks: WASM payload; three.js interop needs vertex and index conversion; smaller user base than three.js; large concave edits may be slow (untested); not a NURBS kernel, so curved .3dm surfaces become meshes.

findings.name: SunCalc + three-mesh-bvh (core sun and shadow)
findings.what_it_does: SunCalc 2.1.1 (BSD-2, 5 Oct 2026): dependency-free sun altitude, azimuth and times from Meeus algorithms (about 0.08 degree error). three-mesh-bvh 0.9.16 (MIT) accelerates raycasts and spatial queries against three.js meshes.
findings.how_we_use_it: Core sun module: SunCalc gives Vancouver sun vectors for solstice and equinox days; BVH raycasts from sample points on neighbouring facades and public realm (15-minute steps) give shadow hours. No Pyodide needed; pvlib stays for irradiance in v1.
findings.popularity: SunCalc 3.5k stars (270k weekly npm); three-mesh-bvh 3.5k (3.0M weekly npm)
findings.saves: Sun module in about 2 person-days (our estimate) with no Python cold start; Bvh helper already ships in drei.
findings.risks: SunCalc v2 was a breaking rewrite; npm lists no licence field (GitHub shows BSD-2). Shadow method is ours, not benchmarked: validate against a published case. Neighbour massing quality limits accuracy.

findings.name: Opaque-origin iframe + hardened CSP sandbox header (community module isolation)
findings.what_it_does: CSP sandbox sent as an HTTP header (not supported in meta) gives a frame an opaque origin. connect-src covers only script network APIs (fetch, XHR, WebSocket, EventSource, sendBeacon, ping), not image loads or WebRTC. Workers share the app origin; QuickJS has no network.
findings.how_we_use_it: Core: first-party modules only. v1: sandbox origin sends sandbox allow-scripts; default-src 'none'; pinned script-src; img-src data: blob:; form-action and base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors app. No allow-same-origin, popups or top-navigation. Third-party code that sees geometry is declarative or QuickJS. Exfiltration tests gate release.
findings.last_activity: MDN pages current; quickjs-emscripten v0.32.0 on 2026-02-16, commit 2026-07-23
findings.saves: Avoids shipping community code that can read stored keys or user geometry; a header-enforced sandbox also covers the page being opened top-level; declarative-first modules cut review time.
findings.risks: MDN's CSP list has no WebRTC directive; DNS prefetch and frame self-navigation untested. Header sandbox on a top-level load, worker-in-sandbox and COEP-with-iframe also untested in Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari. QuickJS unaudited, below 1.0.

findings.name: Cloudflare Workers static assets + key-proxy Worker + AI Gateway
findings.what_it_does: Static assets serve a Vite build free and unlimited, with _headers (100 rules), SPA fallback, and 20,000 files up to 25 MiB on Free. Worker Free: 100k requests/day, 10 ms CPU, network wait excluded. AI Gateway adds logs, caching and gateway-wide rate limits.
findings.how_we_use_it: 1-hour spike by 28 Oct: Vite dist with _headers and SPA fallback, plus an assets-only sandbox Worker. Route the proxy with assets.run_worker_first ['/api/*'] (Wrangler 4.20+), setting CORS and CSP headers in Worker code. Proxy: origin allow-list, Supabase JWT via jose, AI Gateway. GitHub Pages is the fallback.
findings.last_activity: Pages docs updated 2026-08-25; Workers docs current Oct 2026 (SPA page examples use compatibility date 2026-10-21)
findings.saves: Closes four open hosting flags (CSP, COOP/COEP, sandbox header, SPA fallback) with one product; asset requests cost nothing; keys leave the browser in about half a day (our estimate).
findings.risks: Free-plan terms for student use unstated; one more account to secure; _headers on SPA-fallback responses and on assets under run_worker_first untested; navigation requests skip the Worker by default; AI Gateway limits are per gateway, not per user.

findings.name: Supabase (Postgres, Auth with GitHub, Storage, Edge Functions)
findings.what_it_does: Hosted Postgres, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions. Free: 500 MB database, 50k MAU, 1 GB storage, 5 GB egress, 500k function invocations/month, 2 active projects, pause after 1 week idle. Edge Functions on Free: 2 s CPU, 150 s wall clock.
findings.how_we_use_it: v1: GitHub sign-in (GitHub's web OAuth flow needs a client secret, so a static page cannot do it alone), module metadata, saved projects. The Worker verifies Supabase JWTs with jose against the project's JWKS endpoint. Weekly keep-alive GitHub Action. Before that, run static with local storage.
findings.saves: Auth, database, storage and row-level security in about a day; avoids writing a backend; hosts the proxy alternative.
findings.risks: Pauses after 7 days idle; two active projects; use asymmetric signing keys (Supabase discourages local HS256 checks; JWKS cached about 10 min); provider_token for GitHub undocumented; supabase-js needs Node 22+; Pro from $25/month.

findings.name: Claude Citations API (text blocks and PDFs to Batch)
findings.what_it_does: Documents with citations enabled return char, page or block locations plus cited_text (not billed as output). PDF pages cost text plus image tokens; text and custom-content documents carry no image tokens. Works with caching and Batch (50% off); structured outputs return 400.
findings.how_we_use_it: Core: for text-extractable by-laws, extract text locally and send paragraph blocks as custom-content documents (a local table maps block index to page); send PDF pages only for tables or figures. Batch API; commit only citation JSON (locator, short cited_text, URL). Unsourced claims render as editable team assumptions.
findings.popularity: Official docs; all active models support it
findings.saves: No vector database, quote matching or Markdown conversion in core. Sonnet 5.5, 80k-token corpus plus 1k output: $0.17 uncached, $0.21 first cached, $0.018 hit, $0.085 batched (our arithmetic). Text-only blocks drop the image tokens PDFs add.
findings.risks: PDF pages cost 1,500-3,000 text tokens plus image tokens; the newer tokenizer adds about 30% tokens, so run count_tokens on claude-sonnet-5-5. Scans are not citable. Cache writes cost 1.25x or 2x. Haiku 5.5 is 5x dearer above 100k.

findings.name: Docling (with LlamaIndex or Haystack as fallback RAG)
findings.what_it_does: Docling converts PDF, DOCX, HTML and PPTX to structured Markdown or JSON with layout, reading order, tables, OCR; local, MCP server; v2.141.0. Fallbacks: LlamaIndex (MIT, 52.6k stars) CitationQueryEngine numbers sources; Haystack (Apache-2.0, 26.8k stars).
findings.how_we_use_it: v1, not core: convert scanned or long documents (the Citations API cannot cite scans) into committed Markdown with page numbers for chunking and search, human-reviewed. Use LlamaIndex or Haystack only if a module slice outgrows the context or a provider-neutral path is needed.
findings.maintainer: Docling project (LF AI & Data community); LlamaIndex; deepset
findings.saves: Hours of manual transcription per policy document; keeps page provenance; the fallback frameworks save writing retrieval code.
findings.risks: Model downloads and CPU time (sizes not stated); table errors; source-text reuse rights unchecked; LlamaIndex examples assume an OpenAI key and chunk-level citations; Haystack citation component not confirmed on its README.

findings.name: Pyodide (browser Python) + FastAPI local sidecar + pyodide venv CI
findings.what_it_does: Pyodide 314.0.7: CPython 3.14.2 on WebAssembly bundling numpy, pandas, scipy, shapely, matplotlib, pydantic, openai; micropip installs pure-Python wheels; npm pyodide runs on Node. pyodide venv (pyodide-build 0.39.1) runs pytest on Pyodide. FastAPI 0.156.8 is the optional local sidecar.
findings.how_we_use_it: First-party Python modules (pvlib, PyNite, economics) run in a Web Worker: thread isolation, not a security boundary. CI runs tests under CPython 3.13 (use py -3.13; bare python here is 3.9.13) and pyodide venv on Node 24. FastAPI is an optional local sidecar for ifcopenshell (LGPL), OpenStudio and wind.
findings.saves: Removes backend hosting for most analysis; same Python serves CI and browser; Pydantic models double as port-type schemas; venv catches browser-only breakage early.
findings.risks: Multi-MB cold start; no native binaries (Radiance); each package needs a micropip spike; venv allows only pure or pyemscripten wheels and no threads or sockets; Pyodide is Python 3.14, team uses 3.13; free hosted FastAPI has traps.

findings.name: pvlib-python (core), Ladybug Tools (optional, AGPL-3.0) and OpenStudio (roadmap)

findings.name: giscus
findings.what_it_does: Comment widget backed by GitHub Discussions: finds the discussion by pathname, URL, title or term, and the bot creates it on first comment. Needs a public repo, the giscus app installed and Discussions enabled. Themes and reactions; self-hostable.
findings.how_we_use_it: One thread per module id in the module repo's Discussions; commenters sign in with GitHub. giscus cannot apply labels, so a GitHub Action on the discussion_comment event adds the 'false-assumption' label when a keyword appears.
findings.saves: Comments, moderation, notifications and auth backend in about an hour instead of weeks.

principles.principle: Context is a finite budget: keep the smallest high-signal set, and prefer CLIs and language servers over always-loaded tools.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: CLAUDE.md under 200 lines; workflows in skills (loaded on demand; descriptions truncate at 1,536 characters); path-scoped .claude/rules; give Claude file paths, not pasted files; use gh, npm and the playwright CLI before MCP; install typescript-lsp and pyright-lsp (binaries first); keep only Context7 and shadcn MCP enabled; record /context and /usage before and after each plugin; run /skill-doctor monthly; plugins with default LLM hooks (security-guidance) start pattern-only.

principles.principle: The prompt cache is prefix-exact; mid-session changes to model, effort, MCP servers or plugins force a full re-read.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Choose model and effort at session start, avoid toggling MCP or plugins mid-task, /compact only at task boundaries, /clear between unrelated tasks, restart after editing CLAUDE.md; read the 'Prompt cache' line in /usage.

principles.principle: Route models and effort by quality and latency first; thinking cannot be turned off on the 5.5 models, so effort is the output-cost lever.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: opusplan for plan-then-build; Sonnet 5.5 at medium effort (the Claude Code default for 5.5 models) for building; a project subagent named Explore with model: haiku (the built-in uses the main model; Haiku 5.5 needs Claude Code v2.1.293+); CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL is only a default unless CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE=1; Opus for architecture, justified by quality (2x Sonnet price); set effort explicitly in platform API calls (the API models page lists Sonnet 5.5 at high); keep Haiku contexts under 100k tokens.

principles.principle: Own the component code and use boring, well-documented libraries so the model's knowledge plus current docs make first-try output correct.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Stack limited to Vite, React ~19.3, Tailwind, shadcn (Radix base), zustand+zundo, xyflow, three.js/R3F, Plot. No new framework without a recorded reason; pin R3F 9.x with React together and look up post-2025 APIs through Context7.

principles.principle: Licence is architecture: AGPL, MPL, custom licences and silence all shape what can be bundled, copied and hosted; dev tools differ from shipped code.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Keep a licence table for every dependency and cohort tool (2 MIT, 1 all rights reserved, 12 no licence file); decide the platform licence before importing Ladybug (AGPL-3.0); exclude tldraw (custom); keep Pyodide and web-ifc (MPL-2.0) unmodified; copy no unlicensed code; GPL dev tools such as fnm stay out of the bundle.

principles.principle: Static-first, backend-later, secrets never in the bundle; choose the host by the response headers you need (CSP sandbox, COOP/COEP, SPA fallback).
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Ship core static; precompute AI evidence offline; if the 1-hour spike passes, one Cloudflare Workers account holds static assets with _headers, the sandbox origin and the key proxy (run_worker_first for /api/*), else GitHub Pages with hash routing; BYOK opt-in in memory; Supabase in v1 with a keep-alive; Render, Fly and Hugging Face Docker never required.

principles.principle: Treat community content as hostile input: a worker is not a sandbox, chart specs are code-like, isolation must come from headers not meta tags, and connect-src alone does not stop image or WebRTC leaks.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Third-party code runs only in an opaque-origin iframe (or QuickJS) served with sandbox allow-scripts plus default-src 'none', narrow script-src, img-src data: blob:, form-action and base-uri 'none', frame-ancestors for our app; code that receives user geometry is declarative or QuickJS; Vega only as host templates or validated data with vega-functions 6.1.1 or later; every release artefact pinned by sha256.

principles.principle: A registry should be a thin index; code, manifests and versions live in each author's repo.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: registry/modules.json lists id, repo, category and sha256 only; manifest.json in the module repo declares typed ports, sources, assumptions and permissions; installs come from tagged Releases; issues route to module repos.

principles.principle: Evidence belongs in the data path, in one provider-neutral shape: cite through the API, not through prompt wording, and show what is not modelled.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Every module result carries evidence objects (source id, locator page/char/block, cited_text, provider, verified flag). Only Anthropic Citations or a human reviewer can set verified; OpenAI outputs render as editable team assumptions unless re-cited; refuted claims keep the FALSE ASSUMPTION colour; modules without a credible source show 'not modelled'.

principles.principle: Progressive disclosure keeps users focused, the aesthetic is planned and gated before coding, and accessibility is tested, not just judged.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Canvas opens with one example graph and five visible modules; advanced ports, thresholds and sources sit behind expanders; one orchestrated motion moment; write PRODUCT.md and a 4-6 colour token palette first; run frontend-design and an impeccable audit on UI PRs; Playwright plus @axe-core/playwright gate PRs on zero serious violations, visible focus and reduced motion; manual checks stay.

principles.principle: Spend tokens where cache and batch discounts apply, and price cache writes, misses and PDF pages honestly.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Precompute static checks with the Batch API (50% off, stacks with caching); send text-extractable documents as text blocks (no image tokens) and PDFs only for table or figure pages; run count_tokens on claude-sonnet-5-5 first (the 4.7+ tokenizer yields about 30% more tokens); cache only prompts reused within the TTL (5-minute write 1.25x pays back after one hit at 0.05x, 1-hour write 2x after about three calls); model per-call cost before shipping any live AI feature.

principles.principle: Plugins, skills and hooks are supply chain: install few, read them first, and switch off default telemetry, hooks, LLM reviews and binary downloads you did not review.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Allow-list: official-marketplace plugins (typescript-lsp, pyright-lsp, frontend-design, skill-creator, security-guidance with its env set first), anthropics/skills (webapp-testing, mcp-builder), impeccable (--no-hooks every run, telemetry off, binary download reviewed, settings.local.json checked), shadcn skill and MCP, Context7 (Upstash, hosted), Playwright CLI. Read each plugin's hooks.json and installer scripts: they can spend tokens or pip-install packages. Skip claude-mem until audited.

principles.principle: Skills should be short, specific, side-effect-gated and run in a cheap isolated context when they only audit.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: SKILL.md under 500 lines, key use case first in the description, disable-model-invocation: true for anything that publishes or writes to the registry, context: fork with model: haiku for read-only audits (set background: false when the result is needed), test each skill with and without it using skill-creator.

principles.principle: Spike before you commit to an unverified browser, WASM or hosting combination, budget the time, and log the outcome as a flag.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Reserve about 1.5 person-days in the core schedule for 30-60 minute spikes with pass/fail criteria: Workers static assets headers with run_worker_first, sandbox exfiltration tests (image beacon, CSS url(), RTCPeerConnection, window.open, self-navigation), worker-in-sandbox on four browsers, JPEG board export under 10 MB, pvlib and PyNite via micropip, Worker streaming, node -v in both agent shells. Record results in the log; failures become visible flags.

principles.principle: Primary sources beat summaries, and a critic's fix needs the same check as any claim: verify dates, versions, licences and maintenance status from registries, READMEs, commit feeds and advisories.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Source each version and licence claim from npm or PyPI JSON, feeds, LICENSE files or advisories. Prefer a branch commit feed to GitHub pushed_at (zundo: pushed_at 2026-01-30 vs main commit 2025-04-29) and npm publish time to edited release entries (Plot 0.6.17: 2025-02-14). r2 caught the Volta suggestion; r3 caught that the critique's Impeccable CI check cannot see a gitignored file. Forum and blog opinions are signals with a voice count.

recommendations.decision: Adopt Vite 8 + React ~19.3.1 + TypeScript + Tailwind 4 + shadcn/ui (--base radix) + zustand with zundo + @xyflow/react + Observable Plot. Install Node 24.22.1 from the official MSI on both machines (check the SHA-256 in nodejs.org SHASUMS256.txt), commit .node-version, set engines to >=22.12 <25, and group Dependabot updates for react, react-dom, R3F, drei and three.

Node 24 is Maintenance LTS from 2026-10-20 (EOL 2028-04-30), Node 26 turns LTS 2026-10-28 and openai-node lists only Node 22 and 24, so pin the major. R3F 9.8.2 peers react >=19 <19.4 and React is 19.3.1. Node is not installed on this machine: a system-wide MSI should reach Claude Code's PowerShell and Git Bash tools after a restart (verify node -v in both), whereas fnm's README does not cover non-interactive shells. typescript-language-server 6.0.2 needs Node >=22.22.2. zundo's last release is 23 months old (main commit Apr 2025): vendor it or use snapshot undo. shadcn --base radix matches React Flow UI.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: Next.js (static export drops server features, adds RSC concepts); Rete.js (last commit 30 Jun 2025); LiteGraph (original last commit Jan 2024, ComfyUI fork archived Aug 2025); tldraw (custom licence); visx; Netlify (credit-based free plan); Node 26 now; fnm as default (optional, only for a second Node); nvm-windows; Volta (unmaintained); hand-rolled undo before zundo fails.

recommendations.decision: Geometry and site stack: three.js r186 via @react-three/fiber 9.x + drei for the viewport. Core imports: .3dm (rhino3dm worker), OBJ, glTF, plus a parametric block builder. v1: IFC via web-ifc, booleans via manifold-3d. SketchUp and Revit: a documented export convention (OBJ/glTF/IFC); Speckle is roadmap. Site context from Vancouver Open Data via MapLibre.
recommendations.rationale: rhino3dm covers one of five promised formats and neither SketchUp nor Revit has a browser parser. SketchUp's help table lists OBJ export for Go/Pro/Studio and glTF for Pro/Studio; Revit glTF add-ins found are third-party (the free E-verse one targets Revit 2019-2024), so IFC is the safer Revit default. Speckle's free plan (1 project, 3 users, 100 versions) and institution-level academia offer make it a roadmap option. Footprints 2009 have LiDAR heights (OGL-Vancouver). The VTC page offers site plans and a 3D model for download (format unknown until the brief is downloaded): test the importers on them and reorder the .3dm, OBJ and IFC priorities then.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: Speckle as a core dependency; Rhino Compute as a core server; Babylon.js (not evaluated); waiting for a Revit/SketchUp browser parser (none found); hand-digitised neighbours.

recommendations.decision: Hosting, headers and keys: run a 1-hour spike by 28 Oct deploying the Vite build to Cloudflare Workers static assets (_headers, SPA fallback, assets.run_worker_first ['/api/*']) plus a second assets-only Worker for the sandbox origin sending the hardened CSP (sandbox allow-scripts; default-src 'none'; pinned script-src; img-src data: blob:; form-action and base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors app), with exfiltration tests (image beacon, CSS url(), RTCPeerConnection, window.open, self-navigation). If it passes, one account hosts SPA, sandbox and a key-proxy Worker (origin allow-list, Supabase JWT via jose and JWKS, upstream via AI Gateway, provider spend caps, per-user limits in the Worker, CORS and CSP set in Worker code); GitHub Pages hosts docs and is the fallback. No keys in the browser; BYOK opt-in in memory.
recommendations.rationale: Cloudflare says to start new projects with Workers; static asset requests are free and unlimited, _headers allows 100 rules (not applied to Worker-generated responses), SPA fallback serves index.html with 200, Free allows 20,000 files of 25 MiB. Navigation requests skip the Worker unless run_worker_first lists the route (Wrangler 4.20+). MDN: the CSP sandbox directive cannot be set from a meta tag; connect-src covers only script network APIs and the other fetch directives fall back to default-src, while form-action, base-uri and frame-ancestors do not. GitHub Pages documents no custom headers. Worker network wait is excluded from the 10 ms CPU limit. AI Gateway rate-limits per gateway, not per user. GitHub's web OAuth flow needs a client_secret and both vendor SDKs block browser use by default.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: Cloudflare Pages (steered to Workers); GitHub Pages as the sandbox host (no headers); coi-serviceworker as the default (first-load reload); keys in the bundle; BYOK as the only route; connect-src 'none' as the only exfiltration control; Supabase Edge Function as proxy (viable, but the free project pauses after 7 days idle); AI Gateway as the only per-user limiter.

recommendations.decision: Compute client-side first and show 'not modelled' where no credible engine exists: JS sun and shadow now; Pyodide worker for first-party pvlib and PyNite in v1; FastAPI only as an optional local sidecar (ifcopenshell, OpenStudio). Energy: not-modelled card, OpenStudio sidecar on the roadmap. Wind: not-modelled card with editable screening thresholds flagged as team assumptions. Structure: slenderness rule-of-thumb flagged as assumption, PyNite spike. Carbon: user-entered factors flagged, EC3 after its API terms are checked. Weather for pvlib and energy cards: precomputed or user-uploaded EPW, never fetched at runtime. CI runs Python module tests under CPython 3.13 (py -3.13; bare python here is 3.9.13) and under pyodide venv on Node 24.
recommendations.rationale: Pyodide 314.0.7 bundles numpy, scipy and matplotlib; pvlib 0.16.1 (Python 3.11+) has its runtime dependencies bundled per the critique's lock-file check, and PyNite 3.2.0 needs prettytable (pure Python) and numpy>=2.4; both still need a short micropip spike. pyodide venv (pyodide-build 0.39.1, Python >=3.12, Node 24 recommended) runs pytest on Pyodide, closing the 3.13-vs-3.14 gap, but allows only pure or pyemscripten wheels and no threads or sockets. pvlib.iotools needs network access, which browser CORS limits. EPW licences are unresolved (Climate.OneBuilding footer reads all rights reserved; PVGIS reuse terms not found). No open-source in-browser wind or Lawson tool surfaced; OpenFOAM is GPL-3.0 and local-only. Inventing physics burns tokens and breaks the evidence rule.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: Hosted FastAPI as a dependency; Ladybug as the core engine; fake CFD or EUI numbers; Pyodide for the first sun module; testing browser-bound Python only under CPython; committing an EPW whose terms are unknown.

recommendations.decision: Settle the platform licence by about 30 Oct: MIT or Apache-2.0 with pvlib as the core solar engine and Ladybug as an optional AGPL plugin, unless the team deliberately picks AGPL-3.0 for core. Send licence requests to the cohort authors by 24 Oct and track replies; the seed library uses licensed tools only (curbside MIT, stair-core-tool MIT) plus re-implementations.
recommendations.rationale: All 15 cohort tool repos checked via raw LICENSE files on main/master: two MIT, one all rights reserved (vancouver-r3-feasibility-study), twelve with none (including dtmass, Vista, Shading-tool-test, MassShadeLight, massing-studio); the toolkit has no LICENSE. Ladybug repos are AGPL-3.0; React Flow attribution stays by request; tldraw needs a key. Not legal advice; confirm with the instructor.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: Silent copying of unlicensed code; assuming Ladybug is permissive; copying GPL ComfyUI-Manager code; tldraw.

recommendations.decision: Module package, registry and isolation: manifest.json (id, version, category, typed ports with JSON Schema, sources[], assumptions[], permissions, sha256, host-compat) plus SPEC.md; registry/modules.json as a thin index updated by PR; installs from tagged Releases pinned by sha256. Core ships first-party modules only; from v1 community code runs in an opaque-origin iframe from a separate origin with the hardened CSP header (default-src 'none', pinned script-src) or in QuickJS; modules that receive user geometry are declarative or QuickJS only. One giscus thread per module; a GitHub Action labels FALSE ASSUMPTION; contributions go by fork and PR. NodePen's template-plus-document JSON is the model for the graph file.
recommendations.rationale: Mirrors the Obsidian registry and the course's one-JSON-per-tool format. Dedicated workers share the app origin with fetch and IndexedDB: thread isolation, not capability isolation. A header-set sandbox also protects a top-level open, which a meta tag cannot do. connect-src does not cover image loads and MDN's CSP list has no WebRTC directive, so a module that sees geometry could still leak it: QuickJS has no network, and the user is told before a third-party module reads their massing. Worker-in-sandbox support has had browser bugs, so spike it. giscus needs a public repo, the app and Discussions; it cannot set labels; discussion_comment workflows run from the default branch.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: Plain Web Worker as the sandbox; main-thread execution; Supabase-hosted code bundles; install from any git URL; GitHub prefilled new-file URLs for PRs (undocumented); adopting NodePen's viewer as a dependency before a spike; JS sandbox for geometry-handling third-party code.

recommendations.decision: Build evidence once, cite everywhere: for core, extract text from text-based by-law and brief PDFs locally (gitignored), send paragraph blocks as custom-content documents with citations enabled through the Batch API (a local table maps block index to page and section), send PDF pages only where tables or figures must be read, and commit only citation JSON (locator, page, short cited_text, source URL), not full text. Move Docling to v1 for scans, chunking and search. One provider-neutral evidence schema in manifest.json; OpenAI outputs render as team assumptions unless re-cited. No vector database until a module's slice outgrows the context or 100k tokens on Haiku.
recommendations.rationale: The Citations API accepts PDFs, plain text and custom content, returns page, character or block locations, bills no cited_text output, and supports Batch (50% off). A PDF page is processed as text plus image (1,500-3,000 text tokens plus image tokens) and the 4.7+ tokenizer adds about 30% more tokens, so text blocks avoid the image cost. Custom content is not chunked further, so cited_text is the whole block: use paragraph-sized blocks. Plain-text documents are sentence-chunked but locate by character offsets. A 100-page text set is 150k-300k tokens: about $3 for 12 batched Sonnet 5.5 module checks at 240k tokens each (our arithmetic; run count_tokens first). Scanned PDFs are not citable, which is Docling's remaining job. Haiku 5.5 input rises to $0.50 per MTok above 100k tokens. Citations and structured JSON cannot share a call. City terms may restrict republishing by-law text.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: Docling before core; PDF input for text-only by-laws; committing full by-law text before reuse terms are checked; LlamaIndex or pgvector now; prompt-only citation requests; OpenAI-only RAG; whole-corpus live calls for every user action.

recommendations.decision: Presentation: Plot for module cards and boards; Vega-Lite only as host-defined chart templates; ECharts only if a heavy interactive view is proven. Author each board as HTML/CSS and export the competition panels as JPEG with Playwright page.screenshot, looping quality until each file is under 10 MB (terms: JPEG, 10 MB per panel; 1 to 4 panels, count and size set by the brief, not yet read); page.pdf is for team review prints only. AI renders use gpt-image-2.5-sunburst (edits) or -flare (fast), pinned to the dated snapshot, as panels at 1536x1024 or 2560x1440 conditioned on a massing screenshot, upscaled locally with Real-ESRGAN; show a data note before the first render; credit OSM, OpenMapTiles and OGL; boards carry no team names or marks; keep unpublished boards private.
recommendations.rationale: A2 (420 x 594 mm) at 150 dpi is 2480 x 3508 px (8.70 MP) and at 300 dpi 34.8 MP, above gpt-image's 8,294,400 px cap; a 1536 px render on a 140 mm panel is about 279 dpi, 2560 px on 280 mm about 232 dpi (our arithmetic; sizes above 2560x1440 are experimental). Terms: panels are JPEG up to 10 MB, no identifying marks, visuals must not be previously published, AI use not addressed (Buildner advises checking the tool's terms). OpenAI: API data is not used for training by default, image endpoints keep abuse-monitoring logs 30 days, zero retention needs approval and covers the 2.5 models. Per-image dollars for 2.5 are not in the text; use usage tokens ($8 in, $30 out per MTok, half on Batch). Raw community Vega specs have 3 High advisories since Nov 2025.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: PDF-only board export; visx; ECharts as default; single-call full-board render; raw community Vega specs; svg2pdf.js as primary (only needed if a PDF is required); naming models 'gpt-image-2.5' without the sunburst or flare suffix; publishing draft boards in the community before results.

recommendations.decision: Claude Code kit and token practice: install typescript-lsp, pyright-lsp, frontend-design and skill-creator from the official marketplace; security-guidance only with its env set in the committed .claude/settings.json (ENABLE_CODE_SECURITY_REVIEW=0 for pattern warnings, with a manual /security-review on PRs touching the Worker proxy, sandbox or auth; optional Sonnet-pinned commit review); anthropics/skills only for webapp-testing and mcp-builder; impeccable (--no-hooks every run, telemetry false); shadcn skill and MCP; Context7 on demand; Playwright CLI. Commit .claude/ (CLAUDE.md under 200 lines, path-scoped rules, skills, a project Explore subagent on Haiku). Route with opusplan and Sonnet 5.5 at medium effort; /clear between tasks; record /context and /usage before and after each plugin; weekly /usage, /skill-doctor and ccusage review. Write six skills: module-spec-writer, module-scaffold, source-audit, vtc-policy-check, expert-critique-loop, board-export; audit skills use context: fork and model: haiku; publishing skills are manual-only. Add a PreToolUse hook in Node that trims Vitest and Playwright output to failures (jq is not installed).
recommendations.rationale: security-guidance 2.0.15 hooks (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse, Stop): the Stop review uses the newest Opus (up to 3 firings per turn), the commit and push reviewer an Opus alias, and SessionStart may build a venv under ~/.claude/security and pip-install claude-agent-sdk; on a subscription these count against the same limits the team already hit; check ~/.claude/security/log.txt. Opus 5.5 costs $4/$20 per MTok, twice Sonnet 5.5. Fallback config: ENABLE_STOP_REVIEW=0, ENABLE_COMMIT_REVIEW=0, SECURITY_REVIEW_MODEL and SG_AGENTIC_MODEL=claude-sonnet-5-5, commit review on only for sensitive branches via settings.local.json. Impeccable's --no-hooks is per run, and its hook lands in gitignored settings.local.json. pyright-lsp needs pyright-langserver and typescript-lsp needs typescript-language-server: run npm i -g pyright typescript typescript-language-server after Node. Context7 is a third-party (Upstash) hosted MCP. Draft .claude/agents/Explore.md: name Explore; description read-only repo search returning paths and short findings; tools Read, Grep, Glob; model haiku; body says search only, no edits, no code dumps over 20 lines. Draft CLAUDE.md effort table (our proposal): architecture and plan mode opusplan high; building Sonnet medium; mechanical edits and tests Sonnet low; read-only audits Haiku in a fork; UI polish Sonnet medium plus frontend-design. Haiku 5.5 needs Claude Code v2.1.293+.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: security-guidance with defaults (Opus review at every Stop); claude-mem (hosted observer); spec-kit and full Superpowers for now; agent teams (about 7x tokens in plan mode); always-on Playwright MCP; Opus for everything; long CLAUDE.md sections for workflows; installing from awesome lists or third-party marketplace entries without review; Volta or nvm-windows for the Node pin; a CI check for the Impeccable hook (the file is gitignored).

recommendations.decision: Sequence and schedule: by 28 Oct register for the VTC (closes 29 Oct), complete identity verification, download the brief and site pack, read the panel count and size, test the importers on the site model, and send questions before 3 Nov; run the hosting and exfiltration spike. By 13 Nov (core): Vite scaffold, shadcn theme, xyflow canvas with typed ports and executor, zustand+zundo store, manifest schema, three.js viewport with OBJ/glTF (and .3dm if time), SunCalc+BVH sun module, seed modules from licensed code, Plot cards, precomputed citations in a Sources panel, Vitest, deploy, JPEG board spike. By 10 Dec (v1): Worker proxy, Supabase login, giscus, registry PR flow, sandbox iframe, web-ifc, manifold, Pyodide+pvlib, Playwright and axe smoke tests, board export, docs generated from manifests. Roadmap: Yjs 13.6.x, Liveblocks, PGlite, Speckle, OpenStudio sidecar, Starlight, ECharts. Decide the cut list on 24 Oct and re-check on 3 Nov: cut in order the third seed (-1 day), .3dm import (-1, unless the site model is .3dm), Sources polish (-0.5), second seed (-1), Plot cards as plain tables (-0.5), snapshot-only undo instead of zundo (-0.5).
recommendations.rationale: Core estimate is 19.5 person-days plus about 1.5 for spikes, 0.5 for setup (Node, Claude Code, licence admin) and 0.5 for VTC registration, verification and brief reading = 22.0, against 18 working days from 21 Oct to 13 Nov for one person-equivalent (our estimates; 11 Nov is a UBC holiday and lectures are cancelled 9-11 Nov). The six cuts reach 17.5: about zero buffer (a loss of half a day if 11 Nov is off), so anything that slips moves to v1. Terms: teams of 2 to 4, every member verifies identity on Architects' Network before upload. Starlight adds an Astro toolchain (Node 22.22+) for two students; generate docs inside the SPA until outside authors exist.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: Building multiplayer (Yjs, Liveblocks), a registry backend or auth before the canvas and modules work; Starlight or Docusaurus in v1; Next.js or a monorepo toolchain; tldraw sync (custom licence); skipping the spikes to protect build time; leaving registration to the last week.

flags.claim: Community modules are safe when run in a sandboxed Web Worker.
flags.detail: Dedicated workers run on the app origin with fetch, importScripts, WebSocket and IndexedDB; MDN says they are generally not governed by the creator page's CSP (blob: and data: workers are the exception). Thread isolation is not capability isolation, so a worker could read keys or geometry stored in IndexedDB.
flags.correction: Run third-party code in an opaque-origin sandboxed iframe (no allow-same-origin) on a separate origin with CSP connect-src 'none', or in QuickJS-WASM; pin artefacts by sha256; never store keys in IndexedDB or localStorage. Spike worker-in-sandbox per browser. (r3 tightens this: connect-src 'none' alone is not enough, see the r3 flag.)

flags.claim: Vega-Lite specs from the community remove the need to sandbox chart code.

flags.correction: Accept host-defined chart templates plus validated data; if raw specs are ever accepted, schema-validate, block data.url with a custom loader, keep vega-functions 6.1.1 or later and render in the sandbox iframe.

flags.claim: Using vega-interpreter (CSP-safe mode) makes untrusted Vega specs safe.
flags.detail: The GitHub advisory for CVE-2025-66648 states that using vega.expressionInterpreter in CSP-safe mode does not prevent the issue and there is no workaround besides upgrading to vega-functions 6.1.1. vega 6.4.0 depends on vega-functions ~6.2.0.
flags.correction: Treat the interpreter as one layer only: add templates or validated data, a URL-blocking loader, a strict CSP and the sandbox iframe, and keep vega patched.

The _headers docs and the SPA routing page do not say how headers apply to fallback responses (r3: the SPA page does not mention _headers; the headers page says Workers started by run_worker_first need headers set in code and does not say whether assets served under it still get _headers). The docs' filter hook uses bash and jq: write it in Node. Python: see the r3 flag.

flags.claim: security-guidance is a low-overhead addition to a token-saving plugin allow-list.
flags.detail: Plugin 2.0.15 (README, hooks.json, ensure_agent_sdk.py, security_reminder_hook.py opened). Hooks: SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse (Edit/Write and git commit/push) and Stop. By default the Stop diff review runs on the newest Opus (fallback claude-opus-5-5), up to 3 firings per user turn; the agentic commit and push reviewer uses the opus alias (rate limit 20 per hour per session); SessionStart may create ~/.claude/security/agent-sdk-venv and pip-install claude-agent-sdk (skipped when reviews are off, or Python is below 3.10). On a subscription the reviews count against usage limits; on the API path the Stop review is missing from Claude Code cost figures. Opus 5.5 is $4/$20 per MTok, twice Sonnet 5.5.

Alternative: ENABLE_STOP_REVIEW=0, SECURITY_REVIEW_MODEL and SG_AGENTIC_MODEL=claude-sonnet-5-5, commit review only on sensitive branches. Compare /usage and ~/.claude/security/log.txt before and after.

flags.claim: CSP 'sandbox allow-scripts' plus connect-src 'none' keeps community modules from sending data out.
flags.detail: MDN lists connect-src as covering fetch, fetchLater, XHR, WebSocket, EventSource, sendBeacon and a[ping]. Images, fonts, media, frames and workers fall back to default-src, which the r2 plan did not set; form-action, base-uri and frame-ancestors do not fall back.
